chunks: ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام.
About a man who is on a ship: is it permissible for him to place a mat over goods, or over clover, straw, wheat, barley, and other such things, and then perform salat (prayer) on it?
So he said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship; the travel setting in which the ruling applies
key_terms.الشَّعِيرِ: barley; another item mentioned under the mat
key_terms.الْحَصِيرَ: the mat placed as a prayer surface
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةِ: wheat; one of the items mentioned under the mat
key_terms.الْمَتَاعِ: goods or belongings carried on the ship
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; a formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: is it permissible; indicates the legal question being asked

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on a mat placed over goods or grain while on a ship?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) on a ship when ordinary ground is not available. It states that placing a mat over merchandise or similar materials and praying on it is permissible, showing flexibility in worship under practical travel conditions.
